Launched in 2017 by Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman, this Saudi megaproject at the northern tip of the Red Sea was eventually scaled way back amid delays, cost overruns, and criticism — what is it?
Neom: Planned city in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

Nicknamed the 'Demon King of the Sixth Heaven,' this 16th-century samurai is regarded as the first of Japan's three great unifiers, paving the way for retainers Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu — who is he?
Oda Nobunaga: Japanese samurai and warlord (1534–1582)

First championed at an 1900 conference organized by a Trinidadian barrister to protest colonial land theft, this movement seeks unity among indigenous peoples and diaspora descendants of one continent — which movement?
Pan-Africanism: Movement encouraging solidarity among people of African ancestry.

An oligarch who once headed Ukraine's National Bank council, he won the presidency in a 2014 landslide with over 55% in the first round and led the country through the early war in Donbas — who is he?
Petro Poroshenko: President of Ukraine from 2014 to 2019.
Born into the Greek and Danish royal families and exiled as a toddler, he became Britain's longest-serving royal consort after beginning to write to a 13-year-old princess in 1939 — who is he?
Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh: Consort of Elizabeth II from 1952 to 2021.
A Russian colonel general who heads the Chechen Republic, this man took power not long after turning 30, succeeding his assassinated father in the role — who is he?
Ramzan Kadyrov: Head of Chechen Republic since 2007.
As France's Minister of Justice, this lawyer and politician abolished capital punishment there in 1981 under President Mitterrand — who is he?
Robert Badinter: French politician, lawyer and author (1928–2024)
Beginning in October 1990, this conflict pitted the government's army against the Patriotic Front, a refugee-founded rebel force led in part by Paul Kagame, and ran until July 1994 — what was it?
Rwandan Civil War: 1990–1994 armed struggle in Rwanda.
Married for more than 40 years to a celebrated general, this English courtier's close bond with Queen Anne made her one of the most powerful women in early 18th-century Britain — who was she?
Sarah Churchill, Duchess of Marlborough: English noblewoman, courtier and politician (1660–1744)
Growing out of the 19th-century Millerite movement and formally founded in 1863, this denomination observes Saturday as the Sabbath and reveres the writings of co-founder Ellen G. White — what is it?
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
Seventh-day Adventist Church: Protestant Christian denomination.
After finishing third in Turkey's 2023 presidential race, this far-right politician became a so-called kingmaker by throwing his support behind Erdoğan — who is he?
A former professor turned politician, this leader has served in India's upper house of parliament since 2019 and acts as a senior national spokesperson for the Bharatiya Janata Party — who is he?
Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn
Younger brother of a U.S. president and an attorney general, he represented Massachusetts in the Senate from 1962 until his death in 2009 — which long-serving senator?
Ted Kennedy: American lawyer and politician (1932–2009)

Beginning with the death of Russia's last Rurik ruler in 1598 and ending with the Romanov dynasty's rise in 1613, this era of famine, false pretenders, and foreign occupation devastated Russia — what is it called?
Time of Troubles: 1598–1613 chaotic period of Russian history.

This liberal religious tradition has no single creed, instead uniting congregations through shared covenants centered on love and pluralistic worship, drawing on everything from Christianity to Buddhism — which faith tradition?
Unitarian Universalism: Non-creedal liberal religious movement.
The illegitimate son of Mircea I of Wallachia, this nobleman was inducted into the Order of the Dragon in 1431 and twice ruled Wallachia as Voivode in the 1430s and 1440s — who is he?
Vlad II Dracul: Ruler of Wallachia (r. 1436–1442, 1443–1447)
This unofficial coalition of countries officially allied with the United States during the Cold War stood in opposition to the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact — what was this group called?
Western Bloc: Group of states aligned with the United States during the Cold War. The name "Western Bloc" emerged in response to and as the antithesis of its communist counterpart, the Eastern Bloc.
A member of the influential 'Eight Elders' in 1980s China, this revolutionary politician is also the father of the country's current top Communist Party leader — who was he?

Commanding seven 'treasure voyages' across Asia under two Ming emperors, this admiral was a Muslim-born eunuch who received a new surname from the Yongle Emperor — who commanded these historic fleets?
Zheng He: Chinese Admiral and diplomat (1371–1433/1435)
Which of these people was born first?
Joan Clarke (born 1917) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four. It is particularly useful in handling structured data, i.e., data incorporating relations among entities and variables.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Maria Goeppert Mayer is a physicist. In 1986, the Maria Goeppert Mayer Award for early-career women physicists was established in her honor.
Which of these is a chemist?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele is a chemist. Carl Wilhelm Scheele (German: [ˈʃeːlə], Swedish: [ˈɧêːlɛ]; 9 December 1742 – 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.
What is the atomic number of Livermorium?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
What is the atomic number of Polonium?
Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
In what year was Ferruccio Lamborghini born?
Ferruccio Lamborghini: In 1959, he opened an oil burner factory, Lamborghini Bruciatori, which later entered the business of producing air conditioning equipment.
In what year was Josef Mengele born?
Josef Mengele: Before the war, Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine, and he began a career as a researcher.
In what year did Michael Rockefeller die?
Michael Rockefeller: Michael Clark Rockefeller (May 18, 1938; disappeared November 19, 1961) was an American anthropologist and art collector and member of the Rockefeller family.
In what year did Arthur Schopenhauer die?
Arthur Schopenhauer (22 February 1788 – 21 September 1860) was a German philosopher and writer.
In what year did Ludwig Wittgenstein die?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Wittgenstein was born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families.
In what year was Calcium discovered?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
Which company manufactures Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet?
Boeing F/A-18E/F Super Hornet: McDonnell Douglas. The Super Hornet is in service with the armed forces of the United States, Australia, and Kuwait.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15: Soviet Union. The MiG-15 was one of the first successful jet fighters to incorporate swept wings to perform near Mach 1.
Who is credited with discovering Molybdenum?
Molybdenum: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
Who is credited with discovering Serotonin?
Serotonin: Arda Green. It is involved in mood, cognition, reward, learning, memory, and physiological processes such as vomiting and vasoconstriction.
Who is credited with discovering Beryllium?
Beryllium: Louis Nicolas Vauquelin. Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
Stretching from the thoracic diaphragm to the pelvic brim, this body region sits between the chest and the pelvis — which body part?
Abdomen (also belly or stomach in vertebrates, or metasoma in arthropods) is the front part of the torso between the thorax (chest) and pelvis in humans and in other vertebrates.

This Austrian psychotherapist founded a school of psychology emphasizing birth order and belonging, breaking from Freud by proposing that contributing to others is key to a person's sense of worth — who is he?
Alfred Adler (Austrian; February 7, 1870 - May 28, 1937) was an Austrian medical doctor, psychotherapist, and founder of the school of individual psychology.
Its scientific name translates roughly to 'fused lizard,' and it may be the largest of its armored kind at up to 8 tons — which dinosaur genus?
Ankylosaurus is a genus of armored dinosaur. It was named by Barnum Brown in 1908; it is monotypic, containing only A. magniventris.

Around 1920, when the energy source of stars was a complete mystery, which English astrophysicist boldly and correctly guessed it was the fusion of hydrogen into helium — and lent his name to a natural ceiling on a star's brightness?
Arthur Eddington (28 December 1882 - 22 November 1944) was an English astrophysicist and mathematician.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary one-sided facial paralysis of unknown cause can droop an eyebrow, alter taste, and make sounds painfully loud — what is it?
Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
In service with the U.S. Air Force since 1955 — and flown by NASA until 2007 — this subsonic strategic bomber can haul 70,000 pounds of weapons nearly 8,800 miles without refueling. Which aircraft?
Boeing B-52 Stratofortress is an American nuclear-capable subsonic jet-powered strategic bomber.
This Indian physicist discovered, with his student, that light changes wavelength when passing through a transparent material — a phenomenon now named for him — earning a 1930 Nobel Prize. Who is he?
C. V. Raman (7 November 1888 - 21 November 1970) was an Indian physicist known for his work in the field of light scattering.
A flightless ratite native to the tropical forests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this large bird has three living species and lacks a keel on its breastbone — name the bird?
Cassowary (Tok) are flightless birds of the genus Casuarius, in the order Casuariiformes.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
With algorithms and data structures at its core and the theory of computation among its branches, which field studies computation, information, and automation?

Computer science is the study of computation, information, and automation. The theory of computation concerns abstract models of computation and general classes of problems that can be solved using them.
Named after the bladder it was first found in, which amino acid carries a thiol side chain that forms the disulfide bonds holding many proteins together?
Cysteine (symbol Cys or C) is a semiessential proteinogenic amino acid with the formula HSCH2CH(NH2)COOH.
Domesticated over 14,000 years ago — before farming even began — this descendant of wolves shares a common ancestor with the modern gray wolf. What animal is it?
Dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of wolves.
This Russian economist served as Vladimir Putin's economic adviser before becoming governor of her country's central bank, and was ranked among Forbes' most powerful women in 2019 — who is she?
Elvira Nabiullina (born 29 October 1963) is a Russian economist and current governor of the Central Bank of Russia.
This term describes the practice of exposing normally covered body parts to others in public or semi-public settings, whether in person or via a nude photo shared digitally — what is it?
Exhibitionism is the practice of exposing one's intimate parts - such as the breasts, genitals, or buttocks - in a public or semi-public environment.
Sharing the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Maurice Wilkins, this English molecular biologist helped decipher the structure of DNA — who is he?
Francis Crick (8 June 1916 - 28 July 2004) was an English molecular biologist, biophysicist, and neuroscientist.

Built from epithelial tissue with a supporting connective-tissue capsule, this kind of structure secretes hormones straight into the blood if it's ductless, or through a duct to a cavity or surface if not — what is it called?
Gland is a cell or an organ in an animal's body that produces and secretes different substances that the organism needs, either into the bloodstream or into a body cavity or outer surface.

This British businessman and adventurer, chairman of a Dubai-based aircraft brokerage, visited the South Pole multiple times and descended to the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep before dying in 2023 when a submersible imploded in the North Atlantic - name him?
Hamish Harding (24 June 1964 - 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Domesticated in Central Asia around 4000 BCE, this one-toed hoofed mammal evolved over 45 million years from the small, multi-toed Eohippus — what is it?
Horse (Equus ferus caballus) is a domesticated, one-toed, hoofed mammal.

Co-creator of the breakthrough neural network AlexNet and a contributor to landmark AI systems including GPT and AlphaGo, this computer scientist has won a major deep-learning research award three years running — who is he?
Ilya Sutskever (born 1986) is a computer scientist who specializes in machine learning.
An economist-turned-pundit who rose to fame on Argentine TV talk shows, who became the nation's 57th president in 2023 under the banner La Libertad Avanza?
Javier Milei (born 22 October 1970) is an Argentine politician and economist who has served as the 57th president of Argentina since 2023.
This anesthetic drug induces a trance-like dissociative state while preserving breathing, and its S-enantiomer is now used to treat depression — name it?
Ketamine is a cyclohexanone-derived general anesthetic and NMDA receptor antagonist with analgesic and hallucinogenic properties, used medically for anesthesia, depression, and pain management.
With about 180,000 described species — roughly 10% of all known living organisms — which insect order is the second largest, trailing only the beetles?
Lepidoptera are an order of winged insects which include butterflies and moths.
This programming language, whose bytecode interpreter is written in ANSI C, was created in 1993 mainly to let developers extend and customize software — which language?
Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Known by a nickname, this Swedish programmer created Minecraft, the best-selling video game in history, and founded the studio Mojang in 2009 — who is he?
Markus Persson (born 1 June 1979), known by the pseudonym Notch, is a Swedish video game programmer and designer.
This Cuban engineer-turned-politician became his country's top leader in 2021, making him the first head of Cuba since the 1959 revolution who isn't a member of the Castro family — who is he?

Miguel Díaz-Canel (Latin American; born 20 April 1960) is a Cuban politician and engineer who has served as the 8th First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba and the top leader of Cuba since 2021.

Chemically known as bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, this organosulfur compound is a potent alkylating agent and carcinogen with no preventive antidote — protection relies entirely on covering the skin and airways. Name this notorious chemical warfare agent?
Mustard gas are names commonly used for the organosulfur chemical compound bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, which has the chemical structure S(CH2CH2Cl)2, as well as other species.
Catalyzed in nature by iron-bearing nitrogenase enzymes and famously partnered with legumes, this process turns molecular N2 into ammonia — what's it called?
Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which molecular dinitrogen (N2) is converted into ammonia (NH3).
The heaviest living bird, this flightless African species can sprint at 70 km/h and lays the largest eggs of any land animal on Earth — what bird is it?
Favored by royalty in the Chinese Imperial court, this toy dog breed originated in China's ancient capital — name the breed?
Pekingese (also spelled Pekinese) is a breed of toy dog, originating in China.
When this domesticated mammal reached Europe from the Near East, it interbred so freely with local wild boar that scholars still argue whether it's a distinct species — what animal is it?
Pig (Sus domesticus), also called swine (pl.: swine) or hog, is an omnivorous, domesticated, even-toed, hoofed mammal.
A staple food across the world, this tuber is actually an underground stem from a plant in the nightshade family, with wild relatives growing from the southern U.S. all the way to Chile. What is it?
Potato is a starchy tuberous vegetable native to the Americas that is consumed as a staple food in many parts of the world.
Its common side effects read like a list of trade-offs — sedation, weight gain, dry mouth — yet many take this atypical antipsychotic simply to fall asleep — which medication?
Quetiapine (kwi-), sold under the brand name Seroquel among others, is an atypical antipsychotic medication used in the treatment of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depressive disorder.
He'd spent years building and selling theremins toward a Cornell physics PhD before unveiling, in 1964, the first commercial instrument of its kind — which American electronics pioneer was this?
Robert Moog (MOHG; May 23, 1934 - August 21, 2005) was an American electronics engineer and electronic music pioneer.
Spanning continents from North America to temperate Asia, this genus covers the majority of the world's common bushy-tailed squirrels — which genus?
Sciurus (or) contains most of the common, bushy-tailed squirrels in North America, Europe, temperate Asia, Central America and South America.
This Irish mathematician and physicist held Cambridge's Lucasian chair for a record 54 years and lent his name to a theorem in vector calculus and to equations of fluid motion — who was he?
Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet (stohks; 13 August 1819 - 1 February 1903), was an Irish mathematician and physicist.

Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes' and 'kernel,' this genus of spherical, Gram-positive bacteria grows in grape-like clusters and can survive with or without oxygen — what's the genus called?
Staphylococcus (staphul), meaning "bunch of grapes", and (kkkos), meaning "kernel" or "Kermes", is a genus of Gram-positive bacteria in the family Staphylococcaceae from the order Bacillales.
Appointed a government economic minister in 1991, this academic rose to become prime minister of Turkey in 1993 and later served as its foreign minister — who is she?
Tansu Çiller (born 24 May 1946) is a Turkish academic, economist, and politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.

One of the two main forms of inflammatory bowel disease, this long-term condition inflames and ulcerates the colon and rectum, flaring up with abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea before quieting down again — what is it?
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is one of the two types of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with the other type being Crohn's disease.
The largest bird of prey on the Australian continent, distinguished by long broad wings, fully feathered legs, and an unmistakable wedge-shaped tail. What is it?
Wedge-tailed eagle (Aquila audax) is the largest bird of prey in the continent of Australia.
Discovered in 1849 and named for the Greek goddess of health, this nearly spherical body is the fourth-largest object in the main asteroid belt — which asteroid is it?
10 Hygiea: Fourth-largest asteroid. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

Nicknamed 'goutweed' and 'bishop's weed,' this shade-loving carrot-family plant is the type species of its genus and was introduced worldwide as an ornamental, becoming invasive — what is its scientific name?
Aegopodium podagraria: Species of flowering plant in the celery family.
With the general formula CnH2n+2 and every carbon-carbon bond single, methane is the simplest example of this class of hydrocarbons — what's it called?
Alkane: Type of saturated hydrocarbon compound.
First named by Karl Friedrich Burdach in 1822, this paired brain structure tucked in the temporal lobes drives fear, anxiety, and aggression as part of the limbic system. What is it?
Amygdala: Paired structure within the brain temporal lobe.
Unlike fear, which responds to a threat that's already here, this emotional state involves dread over something that hasn't happened yet, often paired with pacing and rumination. What is it?
Native to Eurasia, this perennial plant is grown as a vegetable crop for its tender young shoots, harvested in the spring — what's this vegetable?
Asparagus: Species of flowering plant in the family Asparagaceae.
A Kenyan economist who met his future wife at the University of Hawaii, this man became the father of a future U.S. president and the subject of that son's 1995 memoir — who is he?

With arms and tentacles up to 26 feet long held at right angles to its body, this deep-sea cephalopod has been spotted as deep as 6,212 meters — the only one of its kind known to survive the hadal zone. What is it?

Developed in the 1980s-90s to replace an aging Cold War transport aircraft, this large military cargo plane carries forward the name of two earlier piston-engined predecessors, the C-74 and C-124. What is this modern behemoth called?
Boeing C-17 Globemaster III: American four engine military transport aircraft.

Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide, this oral parafunctional habit — often during sleep and without the person's awareness — can leave you with aching jaw muscles, headaches, and worn-down teeth. What is it?
Bruxism: Grinding or clenching of the teeth.
When this yeast infection strikes the mouth it's commonly called thrush, leaving telltale white patches on the tongue — what is the condition?
Candidiasis: Fungal infection due to any type of Candida.
Responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide in 2020, this condition clouds the eye's lens and causes halos around lights — which condition?
Cataract: Clouding of the lens inside the eye, causing poor vision.
Named for both the tree and its edible nut, this genus of temperate deciduous trees belongs to the beech family — what is it?
Chestnut: Genus of plants. The name also refers to the edible nuts they produce.
Homologous with the male foreskin and developing as part of the labia minora, which fold of skin surrounds and protects the tip of the clitoris?
Clitoral hood: Part of the vulva that covers and protects the glans of the clitoris.
The largest living bird species, this flightless native of Africa is one of just two living species in its genus — which bird?
Common ostrich: Species of flightless bird. The common ostrich is one of two extant species of ostriches, the only living members of the genus Struthio in the ratite group of birds.
Found mainly in muscle and brain tissue, which organic compound helps recycle ATP — its phosphorylated form donating phosphate to ADP to regenerate the body's energy currency?
Creatine: Chemical compound. Creatine ( or) is an organic compound that, in vertebrates, facilitates recycling of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), primarily in muscle and brain tissue.
Most genera in this family of armored, burrowing mammals are extinct — only one genus survives today, with eight living species — which family?

This widely used polar aprotic solvent dissolves both polar and nonpolar compounds, mixes with water, and — once absorbed through the skin — leaves a curious garlic-like taste in the mouth. Which organosulfur compound is it?
Dimethyl sulfoxide: Organosulfur chemical compound used as a solvent.

This movement disorder causes involuntary muscle contractions that twist the body into abnormal postures, and can sometimes be treated with botulinum toxin injections or deep brain stimulation — what is it?
Dystonia: Neurological movement disorder. Dystonia is often intensified or exacerbated by physical activity, and symptoms may progress into adjacent muscles.
Derived from Greek words for 'brain' and 'suffering,' this umbrella medical term covers any disease or disorder that causes overall brain dysfunction — what is it?
Encephalopathy: Disorders or diseases of the brain.
Combining five of mathematics' most fundamental constants — e, i, pi, 1, and 0 — into a single elegant equation, this formula is often called the most beautiful in mathematics. What is it?
Euler's identity: Mathematical equation linking e, i and π.
Carnivora splits into two suborders, dog-like and cat-like — which one groups cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids together?

Passed down through generations rather than taught in a classroom, this field covers oral traditions like legends and proverbs as well as customs like festivals and traditional building styles — what is it called?
Folklore: Expressive culture shared by particular groups.

Named after Scottish naturalist Alexander Garden and first proposed in 1753 by botanist Jane Colden, this fragrant flowering genus in the coffee family is native to Africa, Asia and Australia — which plant genus?
Gardenia: Genus of flowering plants in the coffee family Rubiaceae.
Nicknamed the "silent thief of sight" because it steals vision slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma: Group of eye diseases related to poor retinal and nerve perfusion.
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.
Native to North America, this genus of roughly 50 flowering plant species is better known by its common name — the sunflowers — and includes food crops for humans and livestock alike — which genus?

Helianthus: Genus of flowering plants, the sunflowers. Helianthus is a genus comprising around 50 species of annual and perennial flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae commonly known as sunflowers.
This genus of great apes emerged from Australopithecus and includes modern humans alongside extinct relatives, with chimpanzees and bonobos as its closest living kin — what genus is it?
Homo: Genus of hominins. Homo erectus and Homo neanderthalensis) classified as either ancestral or closely related to modern humans, collectively called archaic humans.

When the thyroid gland churns out too much hormone, the result can be a racing heartbeat, heat intolerance, hand tremor and weight loss — and rarely, a life-threatening 'thyroid storm.' What is this condition?
Hyperthyroidism: Excessive production of thyroid hormone.

Marked by an IQ below 70 and deficits in everyday adaptive skills first apparent in childhood, this neurodevelopmental condition was formerly called 'mental retardation' in the U.S. — what is it now called?
Known as sampaguita in the Philippines, where it's the national flower, this fragrant vine or shrub also lends its blossoms to a beloved variety of tea — which species?
Jasminum sambac: Species of jasmine. Jasminum sambac (Arabian jasmine or Sambac jasmine or Mogra) is a species of jasmine native to Bhutan and India.
Also nicknamed the reed or swamp feline, this solitary wild predator ranges from the Caucasus to Southeast Asia and marks territory by urine spraying — which species?
This severe form of childhood protein malnutrition causes swelling and an enlarged, fatty liver, and is distinct from the calorie-deficient condition known as marasmus — what is it?
Kwashiorkor: Severe protein malnutrition. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.

Originally cultivated by the ancient Egyptians and now grown worldwide with China producing over half the crop, this leafy Asteraceae vegetable also has a stem-focused variety called celtuce — name the vegetable?
Lettuce: Species of annual plant of the daisy family, most often grown as a leaf vegetable.
Genus name meaning 'horned' in Latin, this raptor nests in dense woodland edges but hunts over open ground, feeding mostly on voles — which bird?
Long-eared owl: Species of owl. The genus name, Asio, is Latin for "horned owl", and the specific epithet, otus, is derived from Greek and refers to a small eared owl.
Domesticated some 9,000 years ago in southern Mexico from a wild grass called teosinte, this tall stout grain was once planted beside beans and squash in the Three Sisters trio — what is it?
Maize: Species of grass cultivated as a food crop.

First flown in August 1970 and introduced by American Airlines the following year, this trijet wide-body aircraft has two underwing engines and a third mounted at the base of its tail fin — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas DC-10: Wide-body three-engine airliner.
Sold under the brand name Medrol, this synthetic steroid can trigger iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome if not carefully tapered after high-dose use for acute flares — name the drug?
Famous for mimicking the songs of other birds — and even singing well past midnight — this bird can recognize individual humans and is the state bird of five U.S. states. What kind of bird is it?
Mockingbird: Family of birds. The only mockingbird commonly found in North America is the northern mockingbird.
This autoimmune disease attacks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, often causing drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty swallowing — which condition?
Myasthenia gravis: Autoimmune disease resulting in skeletal muscle weakness.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
This medical condition, defined by a body mass index over 30, is linked to heart disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea — what is it?
Obesity: Medical condition of excess body fat.
This fluid-filled sac that forms within the ovary is usually harmless and often tied to ovulation, appearing as a follicular or corpus luteum type — what is it?
Ovarian cyst: Fluid-filled sac in the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
Best known for creating Gmail, this engineer also built the first prototype of Google's ad platform and once suggested the company's old motto, 'Don't be evil' — who is he?
Known on the street as 'angel dust,' this dissociative anesthetic acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist and can cause hallucinations and psychosis — what is this drug?
Phencyclidine: Dissociative hallucinogenic drug, mostly used recreationally.
Native to Eurasia and temperate Africa but now naturalized worldwide, this flowering plant shares a common name with a banana-like fruit despite being unrelated to it — which species?
Plantago major: Species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae.
Covering the front part of the frontal lobe, this brain region orchestrates higher-order thinking including focus, decision-making, and impulse control — what is it?
Prefrontal cortex: Part of the brain responsible for personality, decision-making, and social behavior.
Emitting beams of radiation from its magnetic poles like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star produces remarkably precise, repeating pulses — what is it?
Pulsar: Type of neutron star with beams of radiation.

A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its status as a separate species has been debated — some call it a coywolf. Name this animal.
Red wolf: Canid native to the southeastern United States. Fish and Wildlife Service recognizes the red wolf as an endangered species and grants it protected status.
A Jesuit priest and polymath from the Republic of Ragusa produced an early precursor of atomic theory and, in 1753, discovered that the Moon has no atmosphere — who was he?
Roger Joseph Boscovich: Croat-Italian physicist and writer (1711–1787)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
